EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical developments of the past 24 hours revolve around heightened tensions between Iran and Israel, coupled with ambiguous and conflicting signals regarding indirect negotiations between Iran and the United States. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz explicitly stated that the IDF is preparing for an independent "Iran War III" with pre-identified targets, should Iran launch ballistic missiles at Israel. Concurrently, maritime activities in the Strait of Hormuz have seen a significant reduction in traffic as Iran asserts new navigational rules and the right to levy service fees, a position that Oman partially supports while affirming commitment to free passage.

IRAN
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a stark warning, stating that the IDF is prepared for an independent "Iran War III" if Iran attacks Israel with ballistic missiles, and has pre-identified targets within Iran. Separately, Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi declared that mine clearance operations in the Strait of Hormuz would be conducted exclusively by Iran, rejecting any French involvement and warning France against "provocative actions." Iran and Oman held their first Joint Committee meeting on the Strait of Hormuz in Muscat to discuss future management and service fees, with Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi expressing support for the concept of "maritime service fees" but affirming commitment to free passage. Shipping traffic through the Strait has significantly decreased in the last two days following reported attacks and US-Iran exchanges.

Regarding the internal political situation, a rare crisis reportedly erupted within Iran's Assembly of Experts over the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the United States. Over 60 members reportedly issued a statement opposing nuclear concessions and calling for punishment of those responsible for the assassination of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. President Masoud Pezeshkian, however, affirmed Iran’s commitment to the MoU if the US adheres to it and stated that no concessions outside national interests have been made. Mohammad Akbarzadeh, Deputy Political Head of the Revolutionary Guard Navy, reportedly died in a "very strange" car accident in Kerman province; some sources suggest he was an opponent of Qalibaf and US negotiations. Armed clashes occurred at a checkpoint in Paveh, Kermanshah province, resulting in the deaths of at least three IRGC members, including Khalid Khalidi, who was allegedly a senior figure in an opposition group and accused of torturing detainees. In Saravan, a family car was attacked, killing the driver and injuring his wife and child, with Press TV attributing the attack to a "US-Israeli-linked terrorist group."

Economically, President Pezeshkian announced that $6 billion of Iran's $12 billion frozen assets in Qatar are slated for release. The US, however, reportedly stated that the full release of frozen assets is contingent on progress in the nuclear issue. Iran’s Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei confirmed that necessary US licenses for oil sales (Clause 10 of the MoU) have been issued and that a technical delegation will travel to Doha to follow up on the implementation of Clause 11 (release of frozen assets), but denied any scheduled direct talks with the US in Doha. Iran’s Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref underscored the urgent need for Iran to achieve "full immunity in cybersecurity" due to persistent enemy threats. Israel's Cyber Directorate reported a threefold increase in Iranian-linked cyberattacks against Israel over the past year.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included a strike on a Hamas tunnel system in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza Strip, which the IDF stated Hamas was attempting to restore in violation of the ceasefire. Additionally, IDF combat engineers completed the sealing of a massive 16-kilometer-long Hamas tunnel system in southern Rafah, which extended 25 meters deep, contained 80 rooms, and served as a command center, and where the remains of Lt. Hadar Goldin were reportedly held for over a decade. This operation utilized over 30,000 cubic meters of concrete. Targeted killings in Gaza included Ismail Masri, head of Hamas’s military security in the Rafah Brigade, and Zaher Abu Salem, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad terrorist involved in the October 7, 2023, attacks and abductions. In southern Lebanon, the Israeli Air Force struck three Hezbollah command centers in Nabatieh and Mayfadoun in response to ongoing attacks, and a Hezbollah rocket launcher was destroyed by a Multi-Domain unit. An IDF reservist soldier was severely wounded by an explosion in Arnoun, southern Lebanon, during operations of the Commando Brigade; the cause is under investigation.

Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel has "no territorial ambitions in Lebanon" but will not withdraw "a millimeter" until Hezbollah is disarmed. He controversially claimed that US pressure, particularly from President Trump, linking the Lebanese and Iranian arenas, prevented the IDF from initiating a "massive" aerial campaign that "would have dismantled Hezbollah." Katz asserted that the IDF has targets in Iran and is prepared to operate independently if Iran attacks Israel with ballistic missiles, warning of a potential "Iran War III." The Israeli government extended the "Special Situation in the Home Front" until July 14 due to "uncertainty in the Iran and Lebanon arenas."

On the domestic front, Justice Minister Yariv Levin called for an end to Prime Minister Netanyahu's trial, suggesting either a pardon or cancellation. The Supreme Court judges reiterated their recommendation to the prosecution to drop the bribery charge in Case 4000 against Netanyahu. The Supreme Court also accepted petitions against the State Comptroller's investigation into the October 7, 2023, events, ruling that parts of it were conducted "without authority." Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced that Israel is prepared to establish three new settlements in the northern Gaza Strip, awaiting Prime Minister Netanyahu's approval. A survey indicated a 37% increase in home burglaries in the first half of 2026, with Tel Aviv seeing a doubling of incidents.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, the IDF carried out an airstrike on a Hamas underground infrastructure in Deir al-Balah after identifying attempts to restore it, calling it a violation of the ceasefire. A significant Hamas tunnel system, over 16 kilometers long and 25 meters deep beneath civilian areas in Rafah (including a UNRWA building), which held the remains of Lt. Hadar Goldin, was sealed by IDF combat engineers using more than 30,000 cubic meters of concrete. The IDF and Shin Bet confirmed the killing of Ismail Masri, head of Hamas's military security in the Rafah Brigade, and Zaher Abu Salem, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad terrorist involved in the October 7 abductions.

Press TV reported a young Palestinian girl was martyred after Israeli warplanes bombed tents in Khan Younis. Another Israeli drone strike in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, reportedly killed two Palestinians and injured 28. Hamas condemned the "world silence over murdered Palestinian children in Gaza" as complicity in genocide. Couples were reported marrying amidst the ruins in Jabalia. An Israeli rights group, B'Tselem, reported that Israeli forces killed Palestinian children in the occupied West Bank in 2025 at the highest rate since 1967. Israel is reportedly rebranding a scheme to displace Palestinians from Gaza from "voluntary migration" to "Free Movement Plan" amid international condemnation. Minister Smotrich announced preparations for the immediate establishment of three settlements in the northern Gaza Strip, awaiting Prime Minister Netanyahu's approval.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations included continued attacks against IDF forces in the security zone in southern Lebanon. An IDF reservist soldier was severely wounded by an explosion in Arnoun, southern Lebanon, during Commando Brigade operations; the cause remains under investigation. IDF Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Hezbollah has 1,200 operatives between the fence and the Litani River, and warned that any attack by Hezbollah on northern settlements would result in an attack on Dahiyeh, Hezbollah's stronghold in Beirut. Katz claimed Hezbollah has a major tunnel system under Ali Taher Ridge, where about 30 operatives are believed to be holed up, and another beneath Beaufort Ridge which the IDF plans to destroy with "500 tons of explosives."

Israeli strikes included the IAF targeting three Hezbollah command centers in Nabatieh and Mayfadoun in response to attacks, and a Multi-Domain unit destroying a Hezbollah rocket launcher. Israeli warplanes were spotted flying low over southern Lebanon, dropping thermal balloons to ignite fires, and struck in Deir Siryan and between Qantara and Deir Siryan. Israeli forces also blew up abandoned residential buildings in Deir Mimas, southern Lebanon.

Diplomatically, CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper met with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in Beirut after the Israel-Lebanon agreement. Reports indicate the Lebanese army is expected to deploy in Zuthr al-Gharbiya and Foron under Cooper's direct supervision. However, Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri rejected the framework agreement with Israel, calling it an "agreement of dictates" that does not preserve Lebanon’s rights. Defense Minister Katz stated that some 600,000 Shiites from southern Lebanese villages and 700,000 from Hezbollah’s Dahiyeh stronghold in Beirut have been displaced. He added that villages along the line of contact in the western and central sectors of southern Lebanon are almost 100% destroyed, and 73% in the eastern sector.

SYRIA & IRAQ
In Syria, IDF forces conducted operations last night in the Al-Abidin village area of Daraa countryside, involving artillery fire and machine gun attacks from a helicopter. The Syrian Foreign Ministry condemned these actions to the UN, calling on the international community to end these "repeated violations." Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Jordan also denounced recent Israeli attacks and military incursions into southern Syria. Militia activity was reported with "Joulani gangs" demolishing homes in Al-Mazra'a village in rural Homs and burning the Sheikh Nasser al-Hakim shrine in Al-Aredha, Homs. UN forces were documented entering Al-Abidin village in Daraa countryside.

In Iraq, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced a September 30 deadline for resistance groups to hand over their weapons to the state, coinciding with the complete withdrawal of coalition forces. This comes amidst US pressure to disarm anti-American factions. The Iraqi Judiciary Council reported the seizure of $11 million and 4 billion Iraqi Dinars during investigations into Ali Ma'arej Swaidij al-Bahadli, the Deputy Oil Minister for Distribution Affairs, and other corruption cases. Armed clashes broke out in Yarmja village in Kirkuk between armed groups and the Iraqi army, and an explosion was reported in Maysan province, with an alleged improvised explosive device targeting a Lebanese hospital there. Heavy drone and helicopter flights were reported over Baghdad and Kirkuk respectively. Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein discussed with the Syrian President the establishment of an oil pipeline. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Karbala and Najaf to discuss arrangements for the funeral ceremonies of the late Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, in Iraq.

GULF STATES
Qatar advised all maritime vessels to temporarily suspend sailing and other maritime activities due to unspecified safety concerns. The Qatari Ministry of Transportation issued a directive for all boat owners and users to temporarily cease sailing and maritime activities from the date of issuance until further notice. Qatar is also facilitating indirect talks between Iran and the US. President Trump is expected to make the inaugural flight of the new Air Force One, gifted by Qatar, on Wednesday to North Dakota.

Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi expressed support for Iran’s plan to impose "maritime service fees" on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz, while also reaffirming Oman's commitment to freedom of navigation and rejection of "transit fees." Oman and Iran held their first Joint Committee on the Strait of Hormuz meeting in Muscat, discussing future management of the Strait in line with mutual interests and international law. Oman and France issued a joint statement reaffirming commitment to international law and the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, though Iran has rejected French involvement in de-mining.

Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Jordan jointly condemned recent Israeli attacks and military incursions into southern Syria. US CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper visited Beirut, meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun following the framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon. Former US National Security Advisor Jake Sullivan suggested that Gulf states might increasingly pursue "exclusive agreements" with Iran for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz, operating outside of US involvement. US CENTCOM maintains a presence of over 50,000 US military personnel stationed in the Middle East. A Bahraini analyst reportedly attributed the Gulf states' protection from Iran to the US presence.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Defense Minister Katz's Iran War III Warning**: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz explicitly stated that the IDF is preparing for an independent "Iran War III" if Iran attacks Israel with ballistic missiles, asserting that the IDF has targets ready in Iran.
2.  **Conflicting Reports on US-Iran Talks**: President Trump claimed Iran requested a meeting in Doha, scheduled for tomorrow, with US envoys Steve Wittkoff and Jared Kushner attending. However, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman and Deputy Foreign Minister denied any direct talks, stating only a technical delegation would go to Doha to implement aspects of the MoU.
3.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions**: Iran asserted its right to impose new rules and charge "maritime service fees" for transit through the Strait of Hormuz, and declared exclusive rights to mine clearance, rejecting French involvement. Shipping traffic has significantly reduced in the past two days.
4.  **Lebanon Escalation and Displacement**: An IDF reservist was severely wounded by an explosion in Arnoun, southern Lebanon. Israeli Air Force struck three Hezbollah command centers in Nabatieh and Mayfadoun. Defense Minister Katz reported 600,000 Shiites displaced from southern Lebanese villages and 700,000 from Beirut's Dahiyeh.
5.  **Gaza Operations and Tunnel Destruction**: The IDF struck a Hamas tunnel system in central Gaza and sealed a 16km Hamas tunnel labyrinth in Rafah where Lt. Hadar Goldin's remains were held. Two senior Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad commanders, Ismail Masri and Zaher Abu Salem, were killed in Israeli strikes.
6.  **Iraqi Disarmament Deadline and Corruption**: The Iraqi Prime Minister set a September 30 deadline for resistance groups to hand over arms, coinciding with the complete withdrawal of coalition forces, amid reports of significant corruption arrests, including a Deputy Oil Minister.
7.  **Iranian Internal Unrest/Attacks**: At least three IRGC members were killed in an armed attack at a checkpoint in Paveh, Kermanshah province. A family car was attacked in Saravan, resulting in one death and two injuries, attributed by Press TV to a "US-Israeli-linked terrorist group."
8.  **Iran's Frozen Assets**: President Pezeshkian announced the release of $6 billion of Iran's $12 billion frozen assets in Qatar, with implementation of oil sales licenses also reportedly underway. The US indicated that the full release of assets is tied to nuclear progress.
9.  **Venezuela Earthquake Disaster**: The official death toll from the Venezuela earthquake has risen to 1,719, with 5,034 injured. The UN is preparing for up to 10,000 fatalities, and Israel is sending a humanitarian aid delegation.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain exceptionally high across multiple theaters. Defense Minister Katz's explicit warning of a potential "Iran War III" and Israel's readiness for independent action against Iran in response to ballistic missile attacks signifies a critical flashpoint. The Strait of Hormuz is an active flashpoint, with Iran asserting new rules and exclusive mine clearance rights, while Oman partially supports "service fees" but remains committed to free passage. A significant reduction in shipping traffic signals increased caution and instability.

Active flashpoints include southern Lebanon, where Hezbollah continues operations against IDF forces, resulting in an IDF reservist being severely wounded by an explosion and ongoing Israeli strikes on Hezbollah command centers. The Gaza Strip also remains active with IDF operations against Hamas infrastructure and commanders, and continued Palestinian casualties. Syria is experiencing spillover effects from the conflict, with Israeli strikes and ongoing militia activity. The Iraqi government's deadline for resistance groups to disarm by September 30, coinciding with the full withdrawal of coalition forces, presents a high-risk internal security flashpoint.

Military posture changes include Israel's extension of the "Special Situation in the Home Front" until July 14, indicating continued preparedness for hostilities, and the IDF's stated readiness for operations in Iran. The US CENTCOM's standing force of over 50,000 personnel in the Middle East underscores regional military readiness. Red lines for Israel include ballistic missile attacks from Iran and Hezbollah attacks on Israeli settlements, which Defense Minister Katz stated would trigger strikes on Dahiyeh. Iran's red lines include any external interference in mine clearance in the Strait of Hormuz.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture is complex. President Trump claimed Iran requested a meeting in Doha, set for tomorrow, with US envoys Wittkoff and Kushner attending. However, Iranian officials denied direct talks, stating only a technical delegation for MoU implementation. The US has indicated that the release of Iran's frozen assets is contingent on nuclear progress. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper met with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in Beirut, following the Israel-Lebanon framework agreement. US Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib demanded an end to US-backed "war crimes" in Lebanon. The US is also pressuring Iraq to disarm resistance groups.

**Gulf States** are navigating the complex regional landscape. Qatar is actively mediating between Iran and the US. Oman held discussions with Iran regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz and expressed conditional support for Iran’s concept of "maritime service fees." Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Jordan issued a joint condemnation of Israeli incursions into southern Syria. Former US NSA Jake Sullivan suggested that individual Gulf states might seek "exclusive agreements" with Iran for safe passage through the Strait, potentially bypassing US involvement.

**EU members** have differing positions. French President Emmanuel Macron's claim of France's willingness to cooperate in de-mining the Strait of Hormuz was firmly rejected by Iran, which warned France against "provocative actions." Spain extended temporary measures to combat the inflationary impact of the Iran war on its economy. Internal EU tensions exist between EC President Ursula von der Leyen and Foreign Affairs Minister Kaja Kallas regarding their stance on Israel.

**Russia** accused Western countries of using "blackmail and pressure" to advance their goals, deeming it a violation of the UN Charter. President Putin acknowledged fuel shortages in Russia due to Ukrainian drone strikes. Russia has also reportedly armed a civilian ship in the Baltic Sea and stated it would take "political and military-technical measures" in response to Finland's plans to amend its nuclear act.

**China** is deepening its strategic cooperation with Belarus, with President Xi Jinping pledging firm support for Belarusian sovereignty. China has also escalated export controls on Japan, adding defense research institutes and industrial units to its blacklist, and grounding private light aircraft nationwide after a crash in Beijing.

**Turkey's** President Erdogan reiterated that the "root of the tensions in the Middle East lies in the Palestinian issue" and called for a two-state solution to achieve lasting peace. The **UN** is preparing for up to 10,000 fatalities from the Venezuela earthquake, with Israel sending a humanitarian aid delegation. Afghanistan reported 38 citizens killed and 163 injured in Pakistani airstrikes along the border against militant hideouts.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the US-Iran meeting in Doha. While President Trump claims Iran requested a meeting and identified it as a direct US-Iran encounter, Iranian Foreign Ministry officials explicitly deny direct talks, stating only a technical delegation will travel to Doha to follow up on specific MoU implementation points. White House reporting suggests a middle ground: US envoys will meet Qatari officials first, and then US and Iranian technical teams will meet *separately* with Qatari and Pakistani mediators, indicating indirect, mediated discussions rather than bilateral negotiations. This discrepancy suggests either a deliberate framing by each side for political leverage or a genuine misunderstanding of the meeting's format.

The situation surrounding "service fees" in the Strait of Hormuz also presents nuanced reporting. While Oman's Foreign Minister expressed support for Iran's plan to discuss such fees, he also affirmed Oman's commitment to freedom of passage and rejection of "transit fees." Former US NSA Jake Sullivan's interpretation of the MoU suggesting Iran could charge fees after 60 days adds another layer, potentially signaling differing understandings or interpretations of the agreement.

Unverified claims include the implication of foul play in the death of Iran's Deputy Political Head of the Revolutionary Guard Navy, Mohammad Akbarzadeh, linking it to his alleged opposition to specific policies. Reports from Omid Dana on specific individuals killed in Paveh and their alleged roles in past protests are not widely corroborated. The attribution by Press TV of the Saravan attack to a "US-Israeli-linked terrorist group" is also an unverified claim.

Propaganda indicators are prevalent across sources. Press TV consistently frames Iranian actions positively and US/Israeli actions negatively, emphasizing Iranian sovereignty and regional influence while condemning alleged "war crimes." Israeli sources, particularly Defense Minister Katz, utilize strong rhetoric to justify military actions and emphasize Israeli strength and resolve, with claims about US pressure preventing Hezbollah's collapse appearing to serve a political narrative. Some Iranian media (Shargh) emphasize the "strategic necessity" of negotiations for Iran ahead of US elections. Channels like Omid Dana display overt anti-regime bias and use emotionally charged language.

Reporting gaps include a lack of precise details on the nature of "attacks" by Hezbollah that prompted Israeli strikes. The exact terms and specific clauses of the "framework agreement" between Israel and Lebanon mentioned by Defense Minister Katz are not fully elaborated, especially in light of Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri's rejection of the agreement. Specifics on the "new rules" for navigation in the Strait of Hormuz asserted by Iran remain vague beyond general statements about fees and de-mining.
